answer_1.quote: We conducted experiments on two representative tasks in natural language generation, which are text generation and machine translation.

answer_2.quote: Specifically, we finetuned two RoBERTa-based classifiers for the evaluations of sentiment and topic. The tense accuracy was evaluated by the same tool adopted in the training set, and we used word-level Copy Success Rate (CSR) to evaluate the lexical constraint. In addition, we used the perplexity (PPL) given by GPT-2 medium and averaged distinctness to evaluate the fluency and diversity of the generated text, respectively.

answer_4.quote: For human evaluation, each sentence received a score of 1 to 5 on sentiment and topic relevance as well as fluency given by three evaluators.
answer_4.guideline: The instruction we provided to them like 'This human evaluation aims to evaluate the model-generated review texts in three aspects: sentiment and topic relevance, and text fluency. All three integer scores are on a scale of 1-5, with a higher degree of topic/sentiment relevance representing a more consistent theme/sentiment, and a higher degree of text fluency representing a more fluent text.'
